ai.title: knowledge.md adds Knowledge Management section and TODO
ai.summary: knowledge.md gains a Knowledge Management subsystem description and file reference. Guidelines shift to plural 'knowledge files' with new comment/documentation rule. TODO replaces error-handling item with 'Try a better diffing strategy?'.

ai.title: Split prompts.ts into main-prompt and generate-diffs-prompt
ai.summary: Refactored backend/src/prompts.ts into two files: backend/src/main-prompt.ts and backend/src/generate-diffs-prompt.ts. mainPrompt now handles the core streaming loop and tool calls, while diff generation logic is isolated. Updated imports in backend/src/server.ts and backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts to reference the new module structure.

eli5.text: The assistant's response engine has been split into two clearer parts: one that manages the live conversation flow and tool usage, and another that handles turning changes into actual file edits. If you watched it work, you wouldn't notice a difference in behavior, but the system now keeps the main chat logic and the file-editing logic in tidy, separate boxes, which should make it easier to maintain behind the scenes.

ai.title: Add Haiku-based diff expansion and sliding window algorithm
ai.summary: New backend module `generate-diffs-haiku.ts` implements `expandNewContent` using Claude Haiku to resolve placeholder comments in shortened diffs, alongside `generateDiffBlocks` using a sliding window match strategy. Knowledge base updated to document `windowSize` trade-offs: larger windows handle scattered changes but degrade performance (O(windowSize^2)) and accuracy. Scope limited to backend diff generation subsystem.

eli5.text: The assistant can now expand shortened code diffs, where unchanged sections were collapsed into placeholder comments, into complete file versions by consulting a new model, using a sliding-window matching technique to compare old and new content. The documentation now explains that larger window sizes catch more scattered changes but cost more processing time and may blur big structural edits, and teams are advised to test different sizes for their codebase. This improves the accuracy of showing exactly which lines changed during collaborative coding sessions, so reviewers see fewer ambiguous gaps in the diff.

ai.title: Add file-specific knowledge files to system prompt
ai.summary: System prompt updated to support file-specific knowledge files alongside directory-level ones. Agents now create `<filename>.knowledge.md` for granular context, while `knowledge.md` remains for directory scopes. This change resides in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`. Exclusion rule for single-file documentation explicitly directs users to the new file-specific format.

eli5.text: The helpful assistant you work with can now tuck away little reminders not just for whole folders of files, but for individual files, too. Before, it had only one big note card per folder called 'knowledge.md'; now it can also make a separate note card right next to a single file, naming it after that file with an extra '.knowledge.md' tag. If you watch it working, you'll see it start dropping these single-file notes in addition to the folder ones, while the folder notes keep doing their old job.

ai.title: Exclude mock-data from backend tsconfig
ai.summary: Added `exclude` rule to `backend/tsconfig.json` to ignore `src/**/__mock-data__/**/*`. Prevents TypeScript compiler errors from test mock files. Internal build configuration update.

eli5.text: The build system now ignores test-only sample files when putting together the backend code, so it no longer trips over placeholder data meant only for testing. This affects the internal build process and won't be visible to you as a user, but it keeps the code-assembly step from stumbling if you were to rebuild the backend locally. The mock-data files themselves still exist and run during tests exactly as before.

ai.title: Refactor diff generation to patch-based expansion
ai.summary: Replaced `generate-diffs-haiku.ts` with `generate-diffs-via-expansion.ts`, introducing `generatePatch` that uses `diff.createPatch` after LLM expansion. Added `openai.ts` wrapper for `gpt-4o` chat completions. Updated `backend/package.json` with `openai`, `diff`, and `@types/diff` dependencies. Expansion prompt now enforces exact line copying and handles trailing brackets.

eli5.text: The backend now uses a new approach to generate code changes: instead of comparing files directly, it asks an AI assistant (GPT-4o) to rewrite a shortened version of your file into full code, then creates a clean, patch-style update that's easy to review and apply. If you're an internal developer or someone reviewing automated code changes, you'll notice the updates now come as precise patches showing exactly what changed, rather than messy full-file comparisons. This makes it easier to see what the system intends to modify and reduces noise in code reviews.

ai.title: Rename WebSocketClient to ChatClient
ai.summary: Renamed `WebSocketClient` class and `websocket-client.ts` file to `ChatClient` and `chat-client.ts`. Updated references in `src/cli.ts` and `src/index.ts` to use the new name. Internal refactor for clarity; no functional changes.

eli5.text: The app renamed an internal helper it uses to talk to the server, changing both the name of that helper and the file it lives in, then updated the few places that called it. You won't notice anything different, the change is purely behind-the-scenes housekeeping to make the code clearer and easier to maintain, with no impact on how the app actually works or feels. Existing functionality remains unchanged since it only renames and restructures code without adding or altering features.

ai.title: Defer file changes to response completion in CLI
ai.summary: File changes are now batched and applied only after the assistant response finishes streaming, replacing the immediate `change-files` WebSocket action with `response-complete`. The `user-input` client action requires a `previousChanges` payload to carry over pending edits across tool-call loops. This affects `backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts`, `common/src/actions.ts`, `src/chat-client.ts`, and `src/cli.ts`. The CLI now prints 'Generating file changes...' on stream end and deduplicates applied changes using `uniqBy` before writing to disk.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to edit a file, those edits now all appear together on your screen at the very end, after the assistant has finished typing its full reply, instead of popping up one at a time while it writes. You'll also see the message 'Generating file changes...' printed when the assistant is done streaming its response, and a final 'Complete!' once every file has been written. This applies to everyone using the command-line chatbot today; behind the scenes, the assistant collects each edit between its questions to you and only saves them to disk as one batch at the end, removing any duplicates first.

ai.title: CLI left/right arrow file version navigation
ai.summary: Left/right arrow keys navigate file versions in CLI chat sessions. `ChatStorage` tracks `FileVersion` snapshots per message; `project-files.ts` adds `getExistingFiles` and `setFiles` for disk sync. Scope limited to `src/chat-storage.ts`, `src/cli.ts`, `src/project-files.ts`.

eli5.text: When you're chatting with the assistant in the command-line version, you can now press the left and right arrow keys to scroll backward and forward through saved snapshots of your project files at different points in the conversation, instead of only seeing the latest state. The system quietly records a copy of each file whenever a new message is sent, and a small helper makes sure the files shown on your screen always match what's written on your hard drive. This only works right now inside the text-based terminal chat, so if you open the project folder and look around you won't notice it yet, but each arrow press switches the view to an earlier or later set of file contents.

ai.title: CLI menu replaced with static ascii art and tips
ai.summary: The interactive chat history menu in `src/menu.ts` and `src/cli.ts` was replaced with a static ASCII art display and usage tips. The `displayMenu` function no longer accepts `ChatStorage` or manages navigation state, simplifying the CLI startup flow. Users now press SPACE to bypass the menu and enter the prompt directly, removing the ability to select or create chats via arrow-key navigation at this stage.

eli5.text: When you start the assistant, you used to see a menu of your saved chats with arrow-key navigation to pick or create one. Now instead you see a simple ASCII art greeting with usage tips, and you press the SPACEBAR to skip straight into typing your next message. The old chat-selection features (scrolling through chats, creating a new one from that screen) are gone from this startup step, so you can no longer manage chats before starting a new conversation.

ai.title: Update CLI prompts and menu tips
ai.summary: src/index.ts prompt adds ESC hint. src/menu.ts changes SPACE action to chat and replaces Tips with TODO. Knowledge.md instruction simplified.

eli5.text: The text you see when you open your assistant has been rewritten. Instead of saying "Press SPACE to continue", it now says "Press SPACE to chat", and the ESC key hint has been added up front so you know the menu shortcut exists without guessing. A tips section was renamed to TODO, and one piece of advice about creating a knowledge file was shortened by dropping the "in any directory" wording. These are small wording changes meant to make the on-screen guidance clearer for anyone launching the assistant today.
